abstraction_design.rationale: The data helpers and card/table components are designed around the app's real variation and stretch well; the per-page not-found/title boilerplate and the home page's separate card builder are the copy-paste you'd pay again when adding an Items section.

findings.issue: The home page rebuilds Pokémon card models (sprite, name, speciesName) separately from cardsFromPokemonRefs (app/app/utils/poke.ts:233-256), forking card/sprite logic
findings.suggestion: Extract a single card builder (e.g. cardFromSpecies) in poke.ts and use it from both the home list and cardsFromPokemonRefs, so sprite/labeling fixes land once

findings.issue: fetchApi/fetchRecord return any, so the shape of API records is re-declared via ad-hoc casts in every page (pokemon/[name].vue:92, moves/[name].vue:12-16, abilities/[name].vue:19-22, types/[name].vue:30-33)
findings.suggestion: Define lightweight interfaces (Pokemon, Move, Ability, TypeRecord) in poke.ts and have the pages consume typed records; shape changes then surface in one module

findings.issue: The not-found handling (useRequestEvent + node.res.statusCode = 404 plus the fallback 'Not found – Pokédex' title) is duplicated in five files (moves:36-37, abilities:31-32, types:45-46, components/NotFound.vue:4-5)
findings.suggestion: Use throw createError({ statusCode: 404 }) inside the useAsyncData handler or a small shared composable (useNotFoundPage(data)) so the behavior and title live in one place

findings.issue: The default API base URL is duplicated between nuxt.config.ts and poke.ts:47, and three files participate in resolving it (config, plugin, data layer)
findings.suggestion: Keep the default in nuxt.config.ts only and let the plugin be the single writer of the data-layer value

findings.issue: Module-level mutable singleton resolvedApiBase plus a process-wide promise cache is implicit shared state across all server requests
findings.suggestion: Acceptable and documented, but prefer passing a config-scoped fetcher (or useRuntimeConfig at the call site) if requests ever need per-request bases

findings.issue: typeEn is serialized as a plain-object copy of the type index purely to survive the useAsyncData payload, then indexed again at line 151
findings.suggestion: Add an englishTypeName(name) helper backed by the cached type index (with the record fetched on demand) instead of copying the map into each page payload

findings.issue: vue and vue-router are listed as direct dependencies although the app imports neither directly (only Nuxt auto-imports)
findings.suggestion: Drop them; nuxt manages these versions and pinning both invites drift

findings.issue: hasLevel boolean prop switches the column set; a second per-table variation would start growing flags
findings.suggestion: Minor: consider passing the column list from the page, or keep the flag but name the abstraction if another column variant appears

summary: This is a tidy, idiomatic Nuxt 4 app: features map one-to-one to route files, shared logic sits in a single well-commented data layer, and the three reusable components take explicit props. Its main editability cost is duplication at the edges — the home page forks card construction from the shared builder, API shapes are untyped and re-cast in every page, and the not-found/title scaffold is copy-pasted five times. Everyday changes are easy; the two-places fixes and a fifth copy of page scaffolding for an Items section are what keep it from being exemplary.
